content_voiceover: This table compares the two major TPO receptor agonists, eltrombopag and romiplostim, and the dosing details here are classic board fodder. Eltrombopag is an oral pill taken once daily, starting at 50 milligrams, but critically, East Asian patients need a lower starting dose of 25 milligrams and a lower maximum of 50 milligrams instead of 75, because of pharmacogenomic differences in drug clearance that raise plasma concentrations at any given dose in that population, that East Asian dosing distinction is a frequently tested detail. Romiplostim, by contrast, is subcutaneous, given once weekly, and titrated between 1 and 10 micrograms per kilogram based on the platelet count response. Pharmacokinetically eltrombopag peaks fast, in 2 to 6 hours, with a half-life of about 26 to 35 hours, while romiplostim peaks slower and much more variably, 7 to 50 hours with a median of 14, and has a long, highly variable half-life ranging from 1 to 34 days. Response rates are actually a bit higher for romiplostim, 79 to 88 percent, versus 66 to 81 percent for eltrombopag. Side effect profiles diverge too, eltrombopag uniquely carries a risk of elevated liver enzymes requiring monitoring, while both agents share headache and confusion, and importantly both carry a risk of bone marrow reticulofibrosis, so bone marrow surveillance is a consideration with either long-term.
keypoints: Eltrombopag: oral once daily; East Asians need lower dose (25mg start, 50mg max)
Romiplostim: subcutaneous once weekly, titrated 1-10 mcg/kg by platelet response
Eltrombopag uniquely risks elevated liver enzymes — monitor LFTs
Both TPO-RAs carry risk of bone marrow reticulofibrosis
